title: At San Clemente, Murād's army of 6,250 destroys the last Castilian field army, 950 men under Ibn al-Khaṭīb, the renegade vizier. 840 of them are killed and 105 taken, for 31 of ours
Morocco makes nine of its new towns on the Strait into a fiefdom under the old rebel name, the 'Kingdom of Sevilla', though Ishbīliyya itself is Granada's. Fās keeps Ronda and Marbella for itself
Qamar, mother of Ismāʿīl ibn Ismāʿīl and of Khālid ibn Yaḥyā, dies of a sudden illness at about fifty-eight
Duʿāʾ bears Sultan Saʿd a son, Ismāʿīl, a month before the peace. He becomes heir to the throne in place of his uncle Ismāʿīl ibn Yūsuf

Peace with Castile. Granada declares its independence, and Castile gives up the land of Niebla and Huelva, six towns from Ayamonte, where Yūsuf died, to Aracena. It also pays a sum into the treasury and owes reparations for ten years. The War of Independence is over

data.gameGlitch: The game put Granada back under Castile as a tributary after the peace; Trent will remove that with the console

source: save of 5 April 1366 (after the peace); Trent's account

title: At the peace the realm holds 62 towns and 732,000 people, 61 of the 72 towns of the Strait's three lands with its ṭāʾifas. The treasury stands at 1,131, with Portugal, Aragon and Castile all paying reparations

The reckoning of the burned south. Between March 1359 and the peace, the lands the armies crossed lost 203,000 people and 125 of Iberia's 424 towns were looted. Extremadura and the lands of Ṭulayṭula each lost nearly a fifth of their people, and the city of Ṭulayṭula a third. The north, which no army reached, grew by 4%
source: saves of 15 March 1359 and 5 April 1366 (tools/devastation.py); Trent asked for the reckoning

title: Qurṭuba becomes an Andalusī city again. In 1349 it held 34,000 Castilians and 6,000 Andalusīs. By the peace the Andalusīs are the larger people, though the city is still mostly Christian
source: save of 5 April 1366 (between the saves of 1 July 1365 and 5 April 1366)

title: The sultan's aunt Maryam bint Ismāʿīl, back at court after three marriages abroad, takes Khālid ibn Yaḥyā's seat in the dīwān and is set to integrating the new lands

Eight days after the peace, the Portuguese south is released as the Ṭāʾifa of al-Gharb: thirteen towns from Silves to Mértola, with its seat at Faro, under Rodrigo of the house of Silves, a Portuguese lord who has embraced Islam. It is Granada's third ṭāʾifa, beside Balansiyya and Mursiyya
source: save of 6 November 1366; Trent's plan of September 1364

title: Five weeks after the peace, Castile begins courting Granada's favour
Qurṭuba of the caliphs is a Muslim city again, the first of the reconquered towns where Islam is the faith of the majority
source: save of 2 October 1366 (between the saves of 5 April and 2 October 1366)

title: The independent realm, seven months on. The army is stood down from fifteen regiments to five and the budget balances (income 67 against expenses 66). The treasury has gone into the land: the silver mines of Qusanṭīna, the farms of Úbeda, and a Great Madrasa rising at Ishbīliyya. Sunnīs and Catholics are exactly even, 308,000 each. The Mamlūk alliance of 1349 is no longer in force. It was still in place on 2 October and disappeared along with the tributary link Trent removed with the console, so it was most likely lost in the fix

data.mamlukAlliance: lapsed between 2 October and 6 November 1366, most likely with the console fix
